0.long_answer: The condition, known as hereditary spastic paraplegia or Strümpell–Lorrain disease, was first described in 1880 by the German neurologist Ernst Adolf Gustav Gottfried von Strümpell. His observation and description of the hereditary nature and the characteristic spasticity of the lower limbs laid the foundation for understanding the disorder. Later, in 1884, French physician Maurice Lorrain provided a more detailed account of the condition, and his name was combined with Strümpell's to form the eponymous designation. Thus, von Strümpell is credited with the initial description of the disease.
